page: Amazon Web Services c8a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 64-bit AMD EPYC 9R45 processors. The instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores mapping directly to 64 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, maintaining a peak clock frequency of 4.5 GHz. Memory configuration comprises 128 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 6 GHz, yielding a 1:2 core-to-memory allocation of 2 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector support includes AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 instruction extensions, alongside AES and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. Networking operates at a 30 Gbps baseline. The instance includes no local storage volumes and no discrete graphics accelerators, delegating data persistence to external network-attached storage.

In synthetic and real-world benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core and single-core computational output. Multi-core stress-ng tests yield 238,555.89 points, while single-core execution reaches 3,753.39 points. Geekbench evaluation registers scores of 2,825 for single-core and 30,892 for multi-core processing, accompanied by strong results in Clang software compilation and ray tracing. Memory throughput registers 412.39 GB/sec read and 185.39 GB/sec write on large 256 MB blocks, paired with top-tier performance in Redis operations and static web serving. Vector capabilities facilitate rapid LLM prompt processing, achieving 6,731 tokens per second on 135M parameter models.

The dedicated physical-to-virtual core model prevents noisy-neighbor latency spikes and eliminates CPU pipeline contention common in multithreaded systems. However, the low memory density of 2 GB per core and the absence of onboard NVMe drives mean high-memory databases or IOPS-heavy transactional engines must accommodate external storage latencies and memory bounds. Consequently, the c8a.16xlarge is strategically suited for CPU-bound tasks such as distributed software builds, video rendering, scientific simulations, CPU-based model inference, and large-scale parallel batch processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c8a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R45 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the server delivers 64 physical cores and 64 dedicated vCPUs operating at speeds up to 4.5 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It is provisioned with 128 GB of DDR5 memory at 6 GHz, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2 GB per core. The instance provides 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no integrated GPUs, and includes no local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistent data. Benchmark metrics reflect top-tier CPU and memory performance across stress-ng, Geekbench 6, software compilation, and vector-accelerated matrix operations with AVX-512. The dedicated core allocation eliminates hyperthreading contention, maximizing predictable multi-core throughput. AWS c8a.16xlarge is suited for computationally demanding workloads including distributed software compilation, CPU-based machine learning inference, financial risk modeling, batch processing, and high-concurrency microservices.
